narration: Walk into a rent-to-own store and grab a five-hundred-dollar TV. By the time you make your last payment, you'll have paid fifteen hundred and fifty-four dollars. That's not a typo.
visual: SVG TV with $499 sticker price on screen, animated dollar counter ticking up from $499 to $1,554, 'THE REAL PRICE TAG' text appears below

narration: Here's their trick — instead of showing the total, they pitch weekly payments. Nineteen ninety-nine a week sounds harmless until you multiply it out and see what you're actually agreeing to.
visual: Orange payment card showing '$19.99/week', then '× 78 weeks' appears, equals sign, '$1,554 TOTAL' box animates in with red background

narration: Four point eight million Americans are inside rent-to-own contracts right now. Most signed up during a financial emergency, and the stores know exactly when to find them.
visual: Grid of 40 orange person silhouettes filling in one by one, counter animating up to '4.8M', 'AMERICANS TRAPPED' label below

narration: Run the numbers and it gets uglier. The effective interest rate on most rent-to-own contracts tops one hundred and eighty-three percent — that beats most payday loans. Wild, right?
visual: Animated bar chart: Credit Card 24% (green bar), Payday Loan 150% (amber bar), Rent-to-Own 183% (red bar) — bars grow from baseline

narration: Think the early buyout option saves you? It still costs eighty percent over retail. There's no good deal buried in these contracts — they're engineered to extract the maximum.
visual: Three animated price tags stacking in: 'Retail $499' in green, 'Early Buyout $898' in orange, 'Full Term $1,554' in red with 311% label

narration: Before you ever walk into one of those stores, check credit unions, secondhand apps, or layaway first. Now that you know the real number, you can't unsee it.
visual: Three option boxes slide in: credit union building icon, secondhand price tag icon, layaway calendar icon — 'BETTER OPTIONS' header, 'FOLLOW FOR MONEY FACTS' CTA
